title: HB1232 (2025 Regular): Liability When Means of Self-Defense Prohibited

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Colorado) (gun-policy Stage 5, Colorado); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Colorado text (Introduced (02/11/2025), 2025-02-11; official copy, https://content.leg.colorado.gov/sites/default/files/documents/2025A/bills/2025a_1232_01.pdf)
provenance.note: Introduced version (02/11/2025). Section 2 (C.R.S. 24-10-106(1)(l)) is a cross-reference that supports the same liability. Amendments after introduction are not in the text read (check bill status; this bill may not have passed).

operative_text:
Section 1 (C.R.S. 13-21-134(1)): AS USED IN THIS SECTION, UNLESS THE CONTEXT OTHERWISE REQUIRES, "ARM OF SELF-DEFENSE" MEANS ANY WEAPON FOR OFFENSE; EQUIPMENT AND ARMOR FOR DEFENSE OF A PERSON; AND AMMUNITION, ACCOUTREMENTS, PARTS, AND ACCESSORIES TYPICAL TO MAINTAINING THE FUNCTION AND MOST EFFECTIVE INTENDED USE OF THE WEAPON, EQUIPMENT, OR ARMOR.
Section 1 (C.R.S. 13-21-134(2)(a)): THE OWNER OR PERSON IN CONTROL OF A PROPERTY WHO PROHIBITS A PERSON FROM BRINGING AN ARM OF SELF-DEFENSE ONTO THE PROPERTY IS LIABLE FOR DAMAGES, INCLUDING NONECONOMIC LOSS OR INJURY, FOR ANY HARM SUFFERED BY A PERSON WHILE ON THE PROPERTY THAT COULD HAVE BEEN PREVENTED BY THE PERSON IF THE PERSON HAD THE PERSON'S ARM OF SELF-DEFENSE.
Section 1 (C.R.S. 13-21-134(2)(b)): A HARMED PERSON IS NOT REQUIRED TO SHOW THAT THE PERSON ACTUALLY WOULD HAVE PREVENTED THE HARM BUT FOR THE PROHIBITION ON ARMS OF SELF-DEFENSE ON THE PROPERTY IN ORDER TO ESTABLISH A CLAIM FOR DAMAGES PURSUANT TO THIS SECTION.
Section 1 (C.R.S. 13-21-134(3)(a)): PURSUANT TO SECTION 24-10-106 (1)(l), SOVEREIGN IMMUNITY IN AN ACTION FOR DAMAGES DESCRIBED IN THIS SECTION IS WAIVED BY A PUBLIC ENTITY THAT OWNS OR OPERATES PROPERTY.
